story: ACUASI flew 1,000 km out of Nenana on August 19th carrying human blood for the International Testing Agency. The flight is published, the finding is not.
phase12_candidates: A PRIMARY DOCUMENT THIS ROUTINE CANNOT READ IS A HOLE IN THE CLAIMS GATE. Two scouts lost primary sources to PDFs today, Beat D on the DNR preliminary decision for ADL 234762 and Beat C on the NPFMC Draft 2027 Annual Deployment Plan, and both reported PDF extraction as unavailable because poppler-utils is missing. VERIFIED THIS RUN that the diagnosis is wrong and the fix is cheap: pypdf 6.19.0 is already installed by bootstrap.sh and extracts text correctly (tested against runs/2026-09-17/carousel.pdf, 9 pages, first page text returned clean). What is missing is a way to FETCH a remote pdf and read it, since WebFetch hands back binary. A scripts/fetch_pdf_text.py taking a url, using urllib plus pypdf, adds no new dependency and turns two dead ends into primary sources. Proposed as this run's reactive fix.

sources.yaml refuses_automated_fetch needs two new hosts, BoardDocs (University of Alaska regents packets) and newsminer.com (429 rather than 403), plus the route AROUND federalregister.gov, whose article pages redirect an automated fetch while /api/v1/documents/<num>.json and the raw text endpoint both work. Three scouts rediscovered that route independently today.

director_A.why: The story's strongest asset is one figure that means the opposite of what it looks like. A thousand kilometres that arrived nowhere is a cold number whose second clause does the work, and PUNCH THEN PROOF lets the receipts land one per line underneath it.

director_B.why: Two true things that can't both be comfortable. Everything about this test is documented except the thing it was for. INVERTED PYRAMID puts the hardest fact first and widens, which suits a story whose context is what makes the fact bite.
